mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns due to increased inflation expectations compressing equity valuations. The negative relationship is consistent across the historical data, so the signal is always active.
failure_condition: The correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20d returns is positive in more than 30% of the 3-year rolling windows, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% occurs in 10% of the data, but 20d returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A joint condition of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 290) and elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 4.0%) signals an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition occurs in 15% of the data, but 20d returns are positive in more than 30% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 1.0% QoQ, federal funds rate above 4.0%, and unemployment rate below 3.8%), the market is vulnerable to a hard landing due to excessive tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The late-cycle expansion regime occurs in 20% of the data, but 20d returns are positive in more than 35% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of residential fixed investment (RSAFS) indicates strong housing market activity, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive equity returns. The signal is always active.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS and 20d returns is negative in more than 30% of the 3-year rolling windows, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, which is associated with positive equity returns. The signal is always active.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 60d returns is negative in more than 30% of the 3-year rolling windows, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which is associated with positive equity returns. The signal is always active.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS and 5d returns is negative in more than 30% of the 3-year rolling windows, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 occurs in 10% of the data, but 20d returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.
